newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds rise, FOMC votes no rate move.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds rise, FOMC votes no rate move.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backeds hovered near session highs in afternoon trade following the Federal Reserve's decision to keep short-term interest rates on hold.
The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), the policy-making arm of the Fed, voted on Wednesday to keep the federal funds target rate steady at 5.50 percent.

The Fed last raised rates in March, moving preemptively to stifle future inflation. Most Wall Street analysts and traders had anticipated no rate move at the conclusion of the Fed's July two-day meeting as recent economic data suggested the economy is slowing from a sizzling first quarter.
A Ginnie trader described the FOMC result as "a non-event," since prices barely moved immediately after the announcement.
Late in the session, however, light buying bolstered Ginnie Mae 8.0 percent and 8.5 percent coupons, the trader said.
Discount coupon pass-throughs also performed strongly, picking up as much as 9/32 on the day, another trader said.
"Fifteen year and 30-year discounts had a good day," he said.

In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were up 5/32 at 100-24/32 bid, yielding 96 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note. Comparable Fannie Mae issues gained 6/32 at 100-21/32, and Freddie Mac paper was up 4/32 at 100-26/32.
In Treasury trading, the 10-year Treasury note was up 7/32, yielding 6.41 percent.

The government will release its payrolls report on Thursday at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT. Economists polled by Reuters forecast, on average, that 222,000 new jobs were added to non-farm U.S. payrolls in June.
